messages:
Maya (PM): Quick design question — thinking about making the latency cards in the dashboard draggable and resizable so users can create custom layouts. Wanted to surface a few concerns: accessibility, snap behavior, and how sampling controls behave when a card is small. Thoughts?
Julian (Design): I like the flexibility, but we need clear affordances for keyboard users. Drag handles + a keyboard 'move' mode. Also live region announcements for size/position changes.
Anika (Frontend): Re: sampling: when a card gets <200px height we should collapse the heatmap into a sparkline and expose a "view full" button. That avoids rendering heavy canvases in tiny tiles.
Ravi (Eng-SRE): Performance note: many small heatmaps = many canvas contexts -> memory. We can virtualize rendering and render static PNG thumbnails for tiny tiles, swap to full canvas on hover/focus.
Bea (DevEx): Copy nit: instead of "view full" maybe "Expand" or "Open panel" — short, keyboard-friendly. Also make sure the expand action is reachable by a single Tab.
Julian (Design): Agree on 'Expand'. For snap behavior: propose a 4-column grid with drag snapping and optional freeform mode. Snapping should respect accessibility contrast of the placeholder guides.
Maya (PM): On p95 and axis scaling: If users resize a card horizontally, should the x-axis time range change (auto-zoom) or keep global time window? Use case: team wants small side-by-side for model A vs B comparison.
Anika (Frontend): Keep the global time window by default. Add a tiny time-sync toggle in the card header: [sync icon] "Sync time". If off, the card can do local zoom/selection.
Ravi (Eng-SRE): Implementation detail: local zoom will need a per-card time-range state and interactions with the routing layer for trace linkouts. We should ensure trace links include explicit time params to avoid confusing cross-card nav.
Julian (Design): Accessibility: when cards are unsynced, announce "Card time range independent" in aria-live. Also keyboard users need shortcuts: e.g., select card -> press Z to zoom; Shift+Arrow to nudge time window. We should document these in the shortcuts modal.
Bea (DevEx): Sampling controls copy: current label "Sampling" is vague. Options: "Event sampling", "Trace sampling", or "Heatmap sampling" depending on panel. We can contextualize with a tooltip: "Reduce rendered datapoints to improve responsiveness".
Maya (PM): UX trade: if sampling is on, do we still show p95 badges? They can be noisy if sampled. Maybe overlay a small badge "est." when metrics are sampled.
Julian (Design): Love the "est." badge idea. Visual treatment: small rounded pill with low-contrast background and tooltip "estimated from sample — increase sampling for accuracy". Keep color contrast >= 4.5:1.
Anika (Frontend): CSS sketch for the pill:
```
.pill--estimated { font-size: 12px; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 12px; background: var(--muted-bg); color: var(--muted-foreground); }
```
Make sure focus ring is visible when pill is tabbable.
Ravi (Eng-SRE): Also add a small indicator in metrics telemetry when a card is using sample-based p95 so that alerts can optionally be suppressed or adjusted.
Bea (DevEx): Keyboard flow for drag: focus card -> press D to enter 'drag mode' -> arrow keys move by grid step -> Enter to commit, Esc to cancel. This mirrors other apps and keeps it accessible.
Julian (Design): Microcopy for the drag hint: "Press D to move card, Shift+D to resize". Show a subtle tooltip near focused card.
Maya (PM): UX question: should collapsed cards (sparkline mode) still allow quick expansion via long-press on mobile? We need consistent interactions across touch + keyboard + mouse.
Anika (Frontend): For touch: tap to focus, long-press to open context menu with "Expand", "Sync time", "Sampling". For desktop: hover + keyboard. Keep interactions discoverable.
rollout-bot: Note: A/B rollout plan created for flexible-tiles feature; cohort = 5% of orgs starting next week.
Ravi (Eng-SRE): Ops note: when tiles are movable across workspace columns, save layout as per-team setting, not per-user by default. Allow "pin layout to me" as an option. Saves on config fragmentation.
Bea (DevEx): Accessibility checklist before beta: keyboard drag/resize, ARIA live announcements, tooltip text, contrast check, focus order stable, resize handles large enough for touch. I'll spin a checklist doc.
Julian (Design): I'll put together two mock flows: "grid-snap" and "freeform" and include keyboard overlays. Will also mock the "est." pill states and sampled vs exact p95 examples.
Maya (PM): Great — next steps: Julian to drop mocks by Fri, Anika to prototype thumbnail rendering approach, Ravi to spec telemetry flags, Bea to draft accessibility checklist. We'll sync Mon. Thanks all :rocket:
